scope: Sound playback and acoustic measurement only; candidate tones through 32 kHz and 10 ms pip delivery. No neural hardware integration.
supersedes_for_current_host: Budget_Sound_Only_10ms_2026-10-15.json assumed Windows for the OmniMic bundled software. Its earlier budget is conditional and is not the current Mac purchasing recommendation.

recommendation.playback: Keep the candidate Edifier MR3 and Behringer UMC204HD. Use wired TRS playback from a precomputed continuous sequence.
recommendation.measurement_first_choice: Borrow a calibrated microphone/measurement chain with documented coverage at 32 kHz for initial frequency and level qualification. Access and cost are unknown.
recommendation.budget_raw_recording_candidate: Dodotronic Ultramic192K EVO: native 192 kSa/s USB waveform capture and nominal 95 kHz bandwidth; short-pip timing and relative amplitude recording candidate.
recommendation.calibration_limit: No supplied unit-specific 32 kHz sensitivity/response calibration or calibration service was established for the Ultramic. It does not complete calibrated SPL measurement by itself.
recommendation.OmniMic: Do not select the 499.98 USD OmniMic package solely for its bundled software on this Mac. Its official manual recommends Windows and warns of unreliable Macintosh/Linux use.
recommendation.qualification: USB class compatibility and vendor Mac software listings support a candidate workflow. Actual Mac/macOS, device enumeration, native-rate continuous recording and full acoustic performance remain bench checks.

candidate_parts.condition: Suitable clip/holder for Ultramic body needs confirmation.

candidate_parts.price_evidence: Fresh official product page: 180 EUR and add-to-cart control. Destination-specific tax/shipping/import cost and delivery are unconfirmed.

budget.price_basis: MR3/interface/cable/stand prices were checked earlier in this same research session. Microphone is a fresh official EUR offer. Currencies are not added together.
budget.microphone_allowance_basis: Author-set USD purchasing allowance for the 180 EUR offer; not a live FX conversion or a delivered quote.
budget.calibrated_measurement_budget: Open. Assumes suitable reference access can be borrowed; purchasing or obtaining high-frequency calibration is additional and unquoted.
exclusions: Extra microphone or conditioning required for calibrated measurement
budget.limit: Approximately 800 USD is a planning budget for playback/raw-timing prototyping with reference access borrowed, not a guaranteed full calibrated setup or maximum delivered price.

Mac_workflow: Confirm the intended Mac/macOS can enumerate both USB devices; use appropriate data-capable USB adapters and stable power.
Set and verify each device's native supported format in Audio MIDI Setup. Disable recording enhancements and automatic gain where applicable.

Record untouched Ultramic PCM/WAV continuously with Mac audio software such as Audacity. Play the precomputed 96/192 kSa/s stimulus sequence through the UMC in a separate configured playback stream/process if necessary.
Save waveform files, the stimulus manifest, actual sample rates, gains, channel maps and geometry. Inspect the acoustic sequence and quantify duration, spacing, ringing and event completeness.
Treat the microphone and interface as independent clocks even if both nominally run at 192 kSa/s. A software aggregate device or resampling does not establish shared physical timing.
Use a calibrated 32 kHz-capable reference to establish frequency-dependent levels. A 1 kHz calibrator alone cannot correct unknown 32 kHz response.

ten_ms.status: Digital sample arithmetic is exact. Measured acoustic duration, spacing and stability remain unverified.
ten_ms.frequency_limit: Vendor microphone bandwidth covers 32 kHz nominally; usable MR3 output and calibrated whole-chain response must still be measured.

official_sources.EVO_manual_facts: Manual p2 specifies 192 kSa/s and 95 kHz bandwidth for UM192K; p3 describes standard driverless UAC1.1 USB audio; later pages describe Audacity/raw PCM capture. Generic response plots are not unit calibration.
official_sources.vendor_Mac_evidence: Audacity is explicitly listed under Mac Software. This is not an exact-host hardware verification.

screened_alternative.UMIK_2: Mac-compatible, but its official manual limits supplied calibration to 20 kHz and requires a custom calibration file for accurate ultrasonic measurement. A 192 kHz sample rate alone does not qualify it for calibrated 32 kHz use.

actions: Research and documentation only. No software install, hardware operation, sound playback, purchase, supplier contact, calibration, or achieved 10 ms acoustic result.
